list.description: A webhook is an address another system calls to tell you something happened: order approved, form submitted. When the call arrives, the platform finds the contact and does what you set up.
list.createDescription: It starts in testing: it stores what arrives, so you can see the fields, and does nothing until you activate it.
list.emptyDescription: Create one to get notified by your store, your website or any system that can call an address.
list.noResultsDescription: Try another word, or clear the filters.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?
delete.description: The address stops working right away, and this webhook's actions and history go with it. Anyone still calling gets an error. This can't be undone.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: What happens when a request arrives. Changes right away.

explain.test: Stores what arrived, so you can see the fields, and runs nothing. Good for connecting the other system without worry.
explain.active: Runs the actions on every request: finds the contact, sends the message, starts the flow.
explain.inactive: Only records it in the history. Nothing is stored for the fields, and nothing runs.

changed.active: Active: the actions run on every request
changed.inactive: Off: it only records in the history

mode.needsContact: Before activating, say where the contact's number comes from: without it, every request fails.
mode.saveFirst: Save your changes before activating: otherwise it runs the old actions.

entry.title: Address
entry.description: Paste it in the system that will call. It sends a POST here, preferably in JSON.
entry.sizeLimitHint: Above that, the caller gets a 413 error and nothing is processed. The history keeps up to 100 KB of the body; the actions get all of it.
entry.rateLimitHint: Above that, the caller gets a 429 error and needs to try again shortly.

test.title: Test

hint.test: In testing, nothing runs: the fields show up below in a few seconds.
hint.active: When active, the test is real: it runs the actions, and may send a message to the number in the body.
hint.inactive: When off, the request only goes into the history.

test.signedHere: This page can't sign, because the key isn't on screen: this test will be refused, which is what happens to anyone without the key. To test it signed, use a terminal.
test.signedTerminal: The command takes your key from a variable: set it before running, with the key you saved.
test.invalidJson: That isn't valid JSON. Check the quotes and commas.
test.tooLarge: The body is over 1 MB: it would be refused.
test.confirmDescription: This webhook is active: the test finds or creates the contact in the body and does everything the actions say, including sending messages. To just see the fields, put it in testing.
test.unreachable: It didn't reach the server. Check your connection.

fields.hint: From the last request in testing. Drag a field into a text on the side, or use the + to save it on the contact's record.
fields.hintTouch: From the last request in testing. Use the braces button in each text to choose, or the + to save it on the contact's record.
fields.waitingHint: Send a test: the fields show up here on their own, in a few seconds.
fields.noneHint: Fields are only stored in testing. Put it in testing and send a request, or write it by hand: {{body.name}}.
fields.userFieldAdded: Action added. You still need to choose the field.

template.noMatches: No field with that name. You can write the path by hand, if it hasn't arrived yet.
template.nothingYet: Nothing has arrived yet. Send a test to see the fields, or write the path by hand, like {{body.name}}.

form.title: What to do when it arrives
form.description: The actions run in this order, one after the other. In texts, {{body.x}} becomes the value that arrived.
form.actionRemoved: Action taken off the list. Save to confirm.

notRunning.test: In testing, nothing here runs. Set up the actions calmly, and activate when you're ready.

errors.contactRequired: Say where the number comes from: with the webhook active, every request fails without it.
errors.urlInvalid: Start with http:// or https://, or use a variable.
errors.nothingToDo: Choose a flow or write a message: with neither, this action does nothing.

actions.locked: Fixed: this one finds the conversation, and the others depend on it

contact.title: Identify the contact
contact.description: Finds the conversation by phone number, or creates one if there isn't any.
contact.missing: The number is missing: with the webhook active, every request is failing because of it.
contact.identifierHint: With country and area code. Finds the contact with or without Brazil's ninth digit.
contact.name: Contact's name
contact.nameHint: Updates the name when it comes in different.

startFlow.title: Start flow
startFlow.short: Sends a message and starts a flow.
startFlow.description: Connects the conversation to a channel, turns on automation, sends the message and starts the flow. What arrived stays in {{vars.webhook.body.x}} inside the flow.
startFlow.connectorInactive: The chosen channel is no longer active: the message won't go out through it. Choose another.
startFlow.flowHint: Without a flow, it only sends the message.
startFlow.flowNotPublished: This flow isn't published: until it is, it won't start.
startFlow.flowNoAccess: You don't have access to flows. Someone who does can choose here.
startFlow.textHint: If blank, nothing is sent and the flow just starts.
startFlow.templateEmpty: No approved templates on this channel
startFlow.templateNone: Without a template, nothing is sent: the official WhatsApp API doesn't accept free text to someone who hasn't talked in the last 24 hours.

userField.title: Save to a contact field
userField.short: Stores a value on the contact's record.
userField.description: Stores a value in the chosen custom field, on the contact's record.

code.title: Run code
code.description: Runs a script, and the next actions wait for it to finish. It can take up to 15 seconds.
code.hint: What arrived comes in params, by path: params['body.name'].

http.title: Call another address
http.short: Forwards what arrived to another system.
http.description: Forwards what arrived to another system, with the headers and body you define.
http.urlHint: It must be a public address on the internet, on ports 80, 443, 8080 or 8443.

internal.title: This address will be refused
internal.description: It points inside a network, not to the internet. For safety, the platform never calls internal addresses, like localhost or 192.168.x.x: otherwise anyone could use it to peek at the computers inside. Use a public address; for testing, a public tunnel works.

port.title: This port will be refused
port.description: For safety, the platform only calls ports 80, 443, 8080 and 8443. Use one of those, or leave the port out of the address.

credentials.title: User and password can't go in the address
credentials.description: The platform refuses addresses with a user and password built in, so they don't end up in logs. Send them in a header, like Authorization.

scheme.title: Only http and https
scheme.description: The platform only calls addresses that start with http:// or https://.

http.bodyHint: Without a Content-Type, it goes as JSON.
http.failureHint: If the destination fails, the next actions carry on, and the webhook shows a warning until the next delivery works.

blocks.empty: Nothing in the sequence yet. Start with a text, an image or a document.
blocks.caption: Caption (optional)

signature.title: Signature
signature.description: Without a signature, anyone with the address can call it. With one, only whoever has the key.
signature.switchOn: A request without a valid signature is refused with a 401 error, and stays in the history.
signature.switchOff: Any request to this address is accepted.
signature.howDescription: Send the headers X-Vekoo-Timestamp, with the time in seconds, and X-Vekoo-Signature, with sha256= and the HMAC-SHA256 of "timestamp.body", made with the key. The body must be exactly what goes in the request. The time has a 5-minute tolerance, either way.
signature.turnedOnSameKey: Signing on, with the same key as before
signature.disableDescription: Anyone with the address will be able to call it again. The key stays stored: turning it back on uses the same one.
signature.rotateDescription: The current key stops working right away: any request signed with it is refused until you change it in the calling system.
signature.secretDescription: The other system signs every request with it.
signature.secretWarning: This is the only time it shows in full. If you lose it, the way out is to renew, and then the previous one stops working.

alerts.dismissDescription: Everyone in the organization stops seeing the warning, and the number in the menu goes down. Dismissing doesn't fix anything: if the problem persists, it comes back on the next failure.

detail.notFoundDescription: It may have been deleted. Go back to the list of webhooks.

logs.description: Every request that arrived in the last 90 days: what came in and what the platform did with it.
logs.emptyDescription: Every request that arrives shows up here on its own. Open a webhook and send a test.

outcomes.ran: The caller got 200, and the platform ran the webhook's actions.
outcomes.captured: The caller got 200. The webhook was in testing: the fields were stored, and no action ran.
outcomes.skipped: The caller got 200. The webhook was off: only this record remains.
outcomes.refused: The request was refused with error {{code}}, by the signature: nothing was processed.
outcomes.failed: The caller got 200, but an action failed along the way. The reason is below.

logs.nothingReceived: The request came with no data.
logs.truncated: The body was over 100 KB and wasn't stored here. The actions received the whole body.
logs.headersHint: Headers with secrets, like Authorization, aren't even stored.
